claims.text: Catalytic activity in metastable PtRuFeCoNi shells on {100}-faceted Pd nanocubes is governed by a multielement cocktail effect.
Multielement mixing tunes hydrogen adsorption toward thermoneutral conditions through orbital hybridization and electron transfer.
Electron transfer from Fe to Ru increases Ru's hydrogen-binding ability during HER.
Ru acts as an active site for HER in the PtRuFeCoNi shell.
Coordinated adsorption and desorption at Pt, Co, and Ni sites modulates oxygen-species interactions during HOR.
The initial supports are approximately 16.4–16.8 nm FCC Pd nanocubes enclosed by {100} facets.
The as-synthesized PtRuFeCoNi shell is approximately 1.0 nm thick, equiatomic, randomly mixed, metastable, and FCC.
Precursor injection at 0.8 mL h−1 into oleylamine/1-octadecene at 200°C produces epitaxial quinary alloy shells on Pd nanocubes.
The PtRuFeCoNi shell has a {100}-terminated, square-arranged multielement atomic-layer structure.
Local lattice distortions and composition-dependent adsorption sites arise in the multielement shell.
The disordered metastable shell is kinetically stabilized at electrocatalytic operating temperatures.
Heating can induce local ordering of the shell into L10 or L12 phases.
PtRuFeCoNi should have higher intrinsic HER and HOR activity than commercial Pt/C and the specified alternative alloy shells.
PtRuFeCoNi should degrade less during HER and HOR cycling than commercial Pt/C and the specified alternative alloy shells.
The predicted activity and durability improvements result from optimized hydrogen adsorption.
The mechanism should hold in 0.5 M H2SO4 and 0.1 M KOH below approximately 80°C while the disordered alloy remains kinetically trapped.
Above approximately 200°C, ordering or phase separation may make the proposed mechanism inapplicable.
Initial DFT results support an optimal distribution of hydrogen adsorption free energies in this system.
Operando XAS supports the proposed electron-transfer mechanism.
